details.summary: This is a stellar recipe that perfectly executes the book's philosophy: a quick, accessible, and genuinely delicious dessert that hits every nutritional target without relying on artificial sweeteners or complex techniques.

dimensions.feedback: Lemon, vanilla, maple, and raspberry is a classic, cohesive combination that perfectly balances sweet, tart, and creamy flavors.
Every ingredient listed is correctly used in the instructions, and no unlisted ingredients appear.
The instructions are excellent. They provide a precise time range (4 to 6 minutes), a specific check time (4 minutes), and a clear visual doneness cue (gently bubbling and significantly thickening).
A stovetop fruit-topped pudding is a staple of Modern American home cooking and fits the style perfectly.
Whisking milk, egg, and cornstarch directly on the stovetop is the standard, foolproof technique for making custard or pudding without a water bath.
The computed nutrition values align precisely with the quantities of 1% milk, egg, maple syrup, and fresh berries provided.
The title accurately reflects the dish. The intro is warm, appealing, and wonderfully free of any 'diet', 'detox', or pseudo-medical language.
This is a highly appealing, comforting, and remarkably fast dessert that feels like a genuine treat rather than a compromise.
Successfully supports both conditions: provides dairy and egg protein alongside whole-fruit fiber, while keeping saturated fat low (1.7 g) by intelligently utilizing 1% milk instead of heavy cream.

Added sugar is honest and carefully budgeted (6 g per serving from a single tablespoon of maple syrup). The carbohydrate component (25.9 g) sits beautifully in the target window without dipping into keto territory.
Matches the 'Desserts' chapter flawlessly—dairy- and fruit-forward, meeting all strict macro targets for this tier while delivering a real, satisfying dessert.
A true 10-minute recipe from start to finish. It uses entirely ordinary supermarket ingredients, dirties only one saucepan, and cleverly serves the custard warm to bypass chill time.
